Fixed 2 real bugs found by background audit: FIXTURE SWAP had no undo snapshot (UNDO afterward corrupted unrelated programmer data instead of reverting the swap); stk DUPLICATE/EXTRACT silently dropped the stack's note (and EXTRACT also dropped wrap) on every clone
details: Re-checked the roadmap first: all 7 originally-listed items remain landed. The two long-flagged NEEDS ALIGNMENT items (attribute pools dead for this RGB-only rig; MIDI/OSC Grandmaster Dim disagreeing with MASTER's multiplicative scaling) are still unresolved product decisions -- left untouched again, still waiting on user direction.

Ran a background audit (same 'asymmetric sibling code path' method prior sessions have used) focused on the least-audited recent commits: FIXTURE SWAP, stk NOTE, stk DUPLICATE, stk EXTRACT, and the other newest stk/AT/FADER commands, checking each against undo, SAVE/LOAD SHOW round-trips, and sibling code paths that should behave the same way.

Bug 1 (real, verified live): FIXTURE SWAP <a> <b> (run_command handler, studio_project.py) pops and remaps prog.data entries directly but never called prog._push_undo() first, unlike every sibling command that mutates prog.data from outside Programmer._parse_action (LOAD CUE, PROGRAMMER CAPTURE, PROGRAMMER LOAD, all internal AT ... actions). Concretely: fixture 1 red=100, fixture 2 red=50 -> FIXTURE SWAP 1 2 -> correctly swapped -> UNDO did not revert the swap; it popped the *previous* command's snapshot instead, silently corrupting fixture 2's programmer data (its entry vanished entirely). Fixed with a one-line prog._push_undo() at the top of the handler, mirroring the sibling call sites exactly.

Bug 2 (real, verified live): stk <n> NOTE (the newest command, added this session cycle) put a .note field on stack with a correct backward-compatible on-disk default (''), but neither of the two existing stack-cloning commands copied it to the clone. stk DUPLICATE copied .wrap but not .note; stk EXTRACT copied neither. Concretely: stk 1 set to note='Dark Moody Show', wrap=True -> stk 1 DUPLICATE INTO 2 kept wrap but silently dropped the note; stk 1 EXTRACT 3 INTO 4 dropped both -- a wrap-looping stack silently stopped looping after EXTRACT, and a production note silently vanished after either clone. Fixed by adding the same getattr(...,'wrap'/'note', default) copy already used for other Cue-level fields (note, fx_outfade) to both stack-level clone paths.

Both are pure in-memory logic fixes -- no schema changes. stack.note/.wrap already default correctly for old show files; the undo stack's shape (data/disabled/selection) is untouched by adding the missing _push_undo() call.

Smoke test extended: 2 new checks confirm FIXTURE SWAP followed by UNDO restores both fixtures' pre-swap values (previously it corrupted them); 4 new checks confirm stk EXTRACT and stk DUPLICATE each carry the source stack's note and wrap flag onto the new stack. 353/353 passing (347 previous + 6 new).

Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1; confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run (only this changelog.json was hand-edited, same as every prior session's practice).

entries.summary: Fixed a real bug: stk BACK never cleared LTP-bleed on wrap-around (first cue -> last cue), unlike stk GO which already did this on forward wrap
details: Re-checked the roadmap first: all 7 originally-listed items remain landed. The two open NEEDS ALIGNMENT items (attribute pools dead for this RGB-only rig; MIDI/OSC Grandmaster Dim disagreeing with MASTER's multiplicative scaling) are still unresolved product decisions, not bugs -- left untouched again, still waiting on user direction.

Picked up an item a prior session had explicitly flagged but declined to guess on: 'stack.wrap only clears LTP-bleed state on forward GO wraparound (_stack_go, last cue -> first), not on BACK wraparound (_stack_back has no equivalent check). The documented WRAP behavior only describes the forward/looping case, so this may be deliberate rather than a bug.' Re-read the actual doc comment on stack.wrap ('True = fire cue 1 clean on wrap-around (no LTP bleed)') and confirmed BACK wrapping (first cue -> last cue, via the same `(idx - 1) % len(numbers)` modulo _stack_back already used unconditionally) is exactly as much a wrap-around as GO's last -> first case -- nothing in the doc or design restricts WRAP to the forward direction specifically, and stk BACK already silently wraps regardless of the flag (same as stk GO), so the asymmetry was in the LTP-bleed-clear side effect only, not in whether wrapping happens. Treated this as the same bug class already fixed for GO, not a new product decision, and fixed it rather than re-deferring it a second time.

Fixed by mirroring _stack_go's wrap_occurred tracking in _stack_back: computes prev_idx = (idx - 1) % len(numbers), flags wrap_occurred when idx == 0 and prev_idx == len(numbers) - 1 (i.e. stepping BACK off the first cue lands on the last), and clears fader.layer under the same `if wrap_occurred and self.wrap` guard GO already uses -- identical logic, mirrored direction.

Smoke test extended: 3 new checks on a scratch stack (98, assigned to fader 9) -- BACK from the first cue with WRAP ON clears a sentinel value seeded directly into fader.layer (confirming the new clear-on-wrap path fires), BACK from the first cue with WRAP OFF leaves the sentinel intact (confirming the flag still gates the behavior, same as GO), and BACK from the last cue (no wraparound) with WRAP ON also leaves the sentinel intact (confirming only the actual wrap transition triggers the clear, not every BACK). First test iteration used a bare string as the sentinel value and crashed inside _stack_fire_cue's existing fx_kill cleanup loop (`for fid_vals in fader.layer.values(): fid_vals.pop(...)`), which assumes every fader.layer entry is itself a dict -- that was a test-authoring bug, not a product bug (fader.layer's documented shape is `{fid_str: {channel: value}}`); fixed by seeding the sentinel as a dict instead. 214/214 passing (211 previous + 3 new). Re-ran the full headless smoke test 4 times in a row with no flakes.

No schema or persisted-data changes -- pure logic fix mirroring existing forward-wrap behavior onto the backward case, fully backward compatible with existing shows (stack.wrap already defaults to False, so BACK's new clear-on-wrap branch is a no-op for any stack that hasn't explicitly turned WRAP on). Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1; confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by any test run (only this changelog.json was hand-edited, same as every prior session's practice).

Re-verified with the same harness: fixture_dim_scroll reports its own y_scroll_max=64 (all 6 rows reachable by wheel), right_col’s own overflow is now negligible. Screenshot re-captured post-fix for a visual diff, not just the numbers.

entries.summary: Fixed 2 real dim bugs: GUI fixture-dim slider clamped virtual_dimmer to 100% on almost any drag; AI 'dim' action had no bounds check at all
details: Re-checked the roadmap first: all 7 originally-listed items remain landed. The two previously-flagged NEEDS ALIGNMENT items (attribute pools dead for this RGB-only rig; MIDI/OSC Grandmaster Dim disagreeing with MASTER's multiplicative scaling) are still open product decisions, not bugs -- left untouched again, still waiting on user direction.

Audited the newest, least-tested dim-setting call sites the same way recent sessions have hunted bugs (asymmetric sibling code paths), since MasterFixture.set_dimmer()/SubFixture.set_dimmer() both document 'accepts 0.0 to 1.0' and every other call site (Programmer.set_dimmer, the MIDI/OSC grandmaster set_all_dim, flash_on) respects that -- except two that didn't.

Bug 1 (real, user-facing): the left-column 'fixture dim' quick-set sliders (one per patched tube, GUIEngine._on_fixture_dim_slider) write the correct 0.0-1.0 fraction into programmer_layer, but then called patch.fixtures[fid].set_dimmer(dim * 100) -- passing a 0-100 number into a function that clamps to [0.0, 1.0]. For any slider position above ~1%, master.virtual_dimmer silently became 1.0 regardless of where the slider actually sat. Masked live because programmer_layer['dim'] (the correct value) is read first everywhere DMX is rendered -- but virtual_dimmer is the fallback default read the moment that key is gone (e.g. after CLEAR resets it, or any status line / PATCH LIST print that reads master.virtual_dimmer directly), so a technician could see '100%' reported for a tube they'd actually set to 30%. Fixed by dropping the stray '* 100' -- the slider's dim variable is already the fraction set_dimmer expects.

Bug 2 (defense-in-depth, same class as the earlier HUE SAT/VAL fix): AIEngine.execute()'s 'dim' action took Claude's JSON 'value' field and wrote it straight into programmer_layer with zero clamp -- every other dim setter in the file bounds-checks its input, but this one trusted the model's output completely. Invisible on live output (final DMX render always clamps on the way out) but an out-of-range value would persist verbatim into any RECORDed cue. Clamped to [0.0, 1.0] and also synced master.set_dimmer() on the same loop, matching what Programmer.set_dimmer() and the GUI slider both already do.

Smoke test extended: 3 new checks -- the AI dim action clamping a 5.0 value to 1.0 and a -3.0 value to 0.0 (verified via a throwaway AIEngine instance whose construction needs an API-key string but never calls the network -- only .execute() runs, which is pure local dict logic), and the GUI slider fix verified directly against gui._on_fixture_dim_slider(None, 0.5, 1) asserting virtual_dimmer lands on 0.5, not 1.0. 211/211 passing (208 previous + 3 new). Re-ran the full headless smoke test 4 times in a row with no flakes.

Also found and fixed, incidentally: this session's container had a stale local `main` git branch pointing at an entirely unrelated, disconnected commit history (root commit 5894aa4, 9 commits, last touched 'Visual polish: SF Mono font') that shared no ancestry with origin/main's real history (root commit 613e9eb, the one this file's actual content and every prior changelog entry live on). Reset the local branch pointer to match origin/main before committing -- this only moves a stale local ref, the orphaned commits are untouched and still reachable by hash if ever needed. Not a code change; noting it here since it blocked the first commit attempt and a future session hitting the same stale-ref symptom shouldn't have to re-diagnose it from scratch.

No schema or persisted-data changes -- both fixes are pure logic corrections to existing dim-setting code paths, fully backward compatible with existing shows. First attempt at the paired widths (computed from a formula) actually overflowed the column's real 349px usable width (get_item_rect_size includes the label text, not just the widget box, so the formula undercounted); caught by re-running the pixel harness and looking at the screenshot, not by inspection, and fixed by hand-measuring a safe fixed width (108px) instead of trusting the arithmetic.

Those two changes took the overflow from 224px to 32px (re-measured after each step, not estimated). The remaining 32px came out of real spare viewport budget, not more content-cutting: raised _H_MAIN from 480 to 512 and confirmed by measurement (both dpg.get_y_scroll_max('left_col') and get_y_scroll_max('main') now read exactly 0.0, and the forms row -- the last thing in the window -- still ends at y=1022, comfortably inside the 1040px viewport) that this didn't push anything else off-screen. Also caught and fixed a real clipping bug introduced mid-session by this same work: the first version of the new 'rsp pool' button was 60px wide for an 8-character label and rendered as 'rsp poo' with the trailing letter cut off -- visible only in a pixel crop of the screenshot, not in code review. entries.summary: Fixed a real, screenshot-verified GUI clipping bug in the active-playbacks row; first session with actual pixel access to the console -- also quantified the long-flagged left-column scrollbar overflow with hard numbers
details: This session found a way to actually SEE the GUI instead of only reviewing widget-construction code by hand: Xvfb + LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 lets DearPyGui 2.3.1 render off-screen in this container, and dpg.output_frame_buffer() dumps the real rendered frame to a PNG. Ran the unmodified app (STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1, NOT headless, so gui.build()+gui.run() execute for real) from a throwaway copy of the repo in /tmp with its own copied studio_data/ -- never touched the real studio_data/*.json -- captured a screenshot after ~40 rendered frames, then force-stopped the DearPyGui loop. Every prior session that touched a popup has had to write some version of 'reviewed by hand, no display access to verify' -- this closes that gap for the first time.

Confirmed by screenshot: the 'active playbacks' row in the left column (each assigned fader's [n] stack-name / current-cue-name / time / priority / go / back / stop buttons) had no width budget at all -- stack name and cue name were plain dpg.add_text widgets with only a source-level [:11]/[:10] character slice, sized in characters, not pixels. For any fader whose stack name was long enough (the very first row in the default show, 'Color Show', already did it), the trailing 'stop' button was pushed off the right edge of the fixed-width (349px) child window and rendered cut off / overlapping the column's own scrollbar -- unreadable and, worse, likely unclickable, since DearPyGui doesn't hit-test content clipped by a parent's bounds.

Root cause: dpg.add_text has no pixel-width truncation of its own, so a horizontal row of [variable-width text][variable-width text][5 fixed-width buttons] has no way to guarantee the fixed buttons stay on-screen once the text is longer than expected -- character-count slicing doesn't bound pixel width because the slice length was chosen without knowing the font's rendered width or the actual row budget.

Fixed with a new GUIEngine._fit_text(text, max_w) helper that uses dpg.get_text_size() to truncate to a real pixel budget (adding an ellipsis when it does), plus a per-rebuild budget computed from the live measured width of the playbacks_list child window minus a pixel cost for the trailing buttons -- calibrated empirically against real dpg.get_item_pos()/get_item_rect_size() measurements of the actual widest row in this show (fader 10, stack 'test27', live cue '2: Blue'), not guessed. Also added a hover tooltip showing the untruncated name whenever truncation actually occurs, so the information the pixel budget can't display inline isn't just lost.

Verified two ways, not just by eye: python3 -m py_compile / the 208/208 headless smoke test (unaffected -- this is GUI-only code the smoke test's gui.build() pass exercises structurally but doesn't pixel-measure), AND a repeatable pixel-position check (dpg.get_item_pos on the trailing 'stop' button's tag) confirming it now sits inside the 349px row with margin to spare for both the previously-broken row and the actual longest real row in the default show, before and after the fix, across three iterations of tuning the pixel budget against real measurements rather than a single guess.

While measuring this, also got the first-ever hard number on the separate, previously-guessed-at 'left column may need a scrollbar on 1920x1080' concern flagged by several prior sessions: dpg.get_y_scroll_max('left_col') reports the left column's content overflows its fixed 480px budget by exactly 224px (real content height 704px). The overall window (1040px tall, deliberately trimmed from 1080 for a menu-bar allowance -- see the W,H=1920,1040 comment) only has ~41px of true unused vertical space below the last pools row, nowhere near enough to grow the left column to fit without also growing every panel row below it and overflowing the window. Eliminating the scrollbar for real needs either compacting left-column content by roughly 180px or a structural redesign (e.g. tabs instead of one long stacked column) -- a design decision, not a one-line fix, so NOT attempted here; recorded with real numbers instead of the prior 'unverified, tight for 1920x1080' guesses so whoever tackles it next has an exact target instead of a hunch.

No schema or persisted-data changes -- pure GUI-layout fix, fully backward compatible. Confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by any run (all rendering/measurement happened against a throwaway /tmp copy of the repo + data dir, never the real one).

entries.summary: Fixed a real bug: COPY stk / COPY CUE / MOVE CUE silently dropped a cue's fx_outfade override on every duplicate
details: Re-checked the roadmap first: all 7 originally-listed items remain landed, per this file's own history and direct code inspection. Also re-confirmed the two open NEEDS ALIGNMENT items from prior sessions (attribute pools dead for this RGB-only rig; MIDI/OSC Grandmaster Dim disagreeing with MASTER's multiplicative scaling) are still unresolved product decisions, not bugs -- left untouched, still waiting on user direction, not re-guessed on here.

Ran a background research pass (following the established 'asymmetric sibling code path' pattern that has found most real bugs in this codebase) focused on areas with less recent deep-audit attention: Block 6 Cue/stack, Block 3 Programmer edge cases, FX distribution features, and Block 14 persistence round-trips for recently-added fields.

Found: Cue.fx_outfade (added several sessions ago -- an explicit override for the FX-tail crossfade time on GO, settable via RECORD CUE FXOUTFADE <n> or the cue timing editor, and correctly read by _stack_fire_cue() at cue-fire time) round-trips correctly through save_stacks/load_stacks (SAVE SHOW / LOAD SHOW), but was never copied by any of the three cue-duplication code paths: COPY stk <n> TO stk <m> (whole-stack), COPY CUE <src> TO <dst> (single cue, any of the stk/CUE address forms), and MOVE CUE <src> TO <dst>. All three build a fresh Cue(...) via the constructor (which always sets fx_outfade=None) and then manually copy the fields the constructor doesn't take -- note, data, and (for COPY stk) nothing else -- but fx_outfade was never in that manual copy list. The single-cue COPY path's own comment even says 'deep-copy all data including follow_time/note', naming exactly the fields it thought to carry over and omitting this one.

Concrete failure: RECORD CUE 5 FADE 2 FXOUTFADE 1.5 (or setting FXOUTFADE via the timing editor) gives cue 5 a real, functioning override -- confirmed it changes playback via the existing FXOUTFADE smoke-test check. COPY CUE 5 TO 6, MOVE CUE 5 TO 6, or COPY stk 1 TO stk 2 all then silently reverted the duplicate to auto-computed FX outfade (a short <=1s tail for FX-to-FX, or an instant snap for a static/kill cue) with no warning, diverging from the cue it was copied or moved from.
Fixed by adding the one-line field copy (nc.fx_outfade = src_cue.fx_outfade / dst_cue.fx_outfade = ... / moved.fx_outfade = ...) at all three call sites, matching the pattern already used for note.

Smoke test extended: 3 new checks build a scratch stack (91) with a cue carrying fx_outfade=3.25, then exercise the real run_command() path for COPY stk, single-cue COPY CUE, and MOVE CUE, asserting the duplicated/moved cue's fx_outfade survives in each case. 208/208 passing (205 previous + 3 new).

Separately investigated and did NOT touch (lower confidence, plausibly intentional): stack.wrap only clears LTP-bleed state on forward GO wraparound (_stack_go, last cue -> first), not on BACK wraparound (_stack_back has no equivalent check). The documented WRAP behavior only describes the forward/looping case, so this may be deliberate rather than a bug -- flagging here rather than guessing, in case a future session or the user wants BACK to wrap-clean too.

No schema or persisted-data changes -- fx_outfade was already a valid, defaulted (None) field everywhere else; this only fixes three code paths that were silently discarding an already-existing field during duplication. Fully backward compatible with existing shows. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1; confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

entries.summary: Fixed a bug: MACRO playback had no recursion guard -- a macro that (directly or indirectly) plays itself would hit Python's recursion limit and crash
details: Roadmap re-check: all 7 established roadmap items remain landed (verified against the code, not just prior changelog text) -- GUI polish, manual/glossary popup (the 'keys' popup, '?' button), changelog popup, fader FLASH wired to MIDI, Block 12 AI engine, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool GUI panels. No gaps found there this session.

Continued the established audit pattern of checking the newest, least-tested features for the 'new capability, no guard rail' bug class that recent sessions kept finding in the FREEZE frozen-snapshot branch (now fixed for BLACKOUT/MASTER, SOLO, direct DMX, and PARK). Since that class looked exhausted, moved to the next newest feature not yet audited: MACRO record/playback (commit e9d0107).

Found: MACRO <n> playback runs each recorded command through run_command() with no recursion guard. A macro whose command list contains 'MACRO <n>' referring to itself, or an indirect cycle (macro A plays macro B, which plays macro A), recurses without bound. Nothing in the recording step prevents this -- MACRO STOP saves whatever text was typed verbatim, and a self- or mutually-referential macro is trivial to create by accident (e.g. recording a 'reset everything' macro that itself calls another macro, before realizing the two now reference each other). The result was an uncaught RecursionError: the main command-bar submit handler (_on_cmd_execute) calls self._cmd(raw) with no try/except, unlike the OSC command path which does wrap run_command in try/except -- so a self-referential macro fired from the GUI command line, a MIDI note mapping, or PAGE/fader GO would propagate an unhandled exception out of the DearPyGui callback.

Fixed with a module-level play-stack (_macro_play_stack, alongside the existing _macro_recording state) that tracks slot numbers currently mid-playback. MACRO <n> checks the stack before running: if n is already an ancestor in the current call chain, it returns 'MACRO <n>: blocked -- recursive playback (<chain>)' instead of recursing, naming the full chain so the operator can see exactly which macros reference each other. The stack push/pop is wrapped in try/finally so a blocked or erroring inner macro always leaves the stack clean for the next MACRO command.

Deliberately did not add a generic exception handler around _on_cmd_execute's self._cmd(raw) call as part of this fix -- that would paper over the specific bug (and any other uncaught exception) with a caught-and-ignored error rather than fixing the actual unbounded recursion, and is a bigger change (touching the main command dispatch path) than this session's scope; noting it here as a possible future defensive-hardening item if another unguarded-exception bug turns up in that path.

Smoke test extended: 4 new checks -- direct self-recursion (macro 97 contains 'MACRO 97') and an indirect A->B->A cycle (macros 95/96) both blocked with a 'blocked' result and no exception, plus a check after each that _macro_play_stack was left empty (confirming the finally-based cleanup). 204/204 total now (200 previous + 4 new).

No schema or persisted-data changes -- pure fix to MACRO playback dispatch, fully backward compatible with existing shows and existing macro files (macros.json format unchanged). Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1; confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

Fixed a real safety bug: after the first UNDO, live DMX output silently froze on stale programmer data for the rest of the session
details: Re-audited the roadmap first (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, MIDI-held FLASH, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool panels) -- all confirmed already landed by direct code inspection. Since a surface audit found nothing new, ran a background research pass looking for asymmetric sibling code paths (the pattern that has produced most real bugs in recent sessions) across areas not yet deep-audited: undo/redo, the manual popup vs run_command() parity, ShowFile round-trips, and pool CRUD symmetry.

Found one, in Programmer.undo() (was: `self.data = snap['data']`): OutputState.link_programmer() does not copy the programmer's dict -- it aliases output_state.programmer_layer directly to the *same* dict object as prog.data (`self.programmer_layer = programmer.data`), and the real DMX render path (get_dmx_for_universe) plus the GUI output-monitor panel both read through that alias. undo() restoring a snapshot by rebinding `self.data` to a brand-new dict (the deep-copied undo snapshot) breaks that alias: prog.data now points at the new object while output_state.programmer_layer is left pointing at the old, now-abandoned one. Every programmer edit after that point (new AT/color/dim commands write into the new object) is invisible to real DMX output and the output monitor forever, until the app is restarted.

This is exactly the hazard a prior session's own comment already flags at the startup link_programmer() call ('CLEAR rebinds prog.data -- re-link so programmer_layer points to the fresh empty dict') -- that one-time fix covered CLEAR (which today actually mutates in place via self.data.clear(), so it was never actually at risk) but never touched undo(), which reintroduces the identical rebind hazard on every single UNDO, not just once at startup.

Fixed: undo() now does `self.data.clear(); self.data.update(snap['data'])` (and the same for self.disabled) instead of rebinding, preserving object identity so output_state.programmer_layer stays aliased to prog.data across any number of undos.

Smoke test extended: exercises the real run_command('UNDO') path (not just calling Programmer.undo() directly), asserts values are actually restored, asserts output_state.programmer_layer IS prog.data (object identity) after an undo, and asserts a post-undo edit is visible through the aliased programmer_layer -- the same path real DMX transmit reads from. 106/106 passing (102 previous + 4 new). Verified studio_data/*.json untouched via git status.

NEEDS ALIGNMENT (not changing without direction): while verifying this, also confirmed a second, more ambiguous issue in the same area -- the factory MIDI CC7/CC74 'Grandmaster Dim' mapping and the OSC /gma3/fader/1/1 legacy mapping both route to set_all_dim(), which stamps one absolute dim value into every patched fixture's programmer entry (via the same programmer_layer alias), rather than scaling output proportionally the way the documented MASTER <pct> command and BLACKOUT do (output_state.master_level, a multiplicative scalar). The two 'master' controls can silently disagree, and set_all_dim would bake a uniform full-patch dim into anything RECORD CUE captures afterward. This looks like it may be a vestigial control from before MASTER existed, kept for backward compatibility with existing MIDI/OSC templates -- but changing its behavior (e.g. to scale like MASTER does) is a product decision about what a physical dim knob should do to per-fixture looks, not a bug fix, so flagging here instead of guessing.
No schema or persisted-data changes -- pure bugfix in existing undo logic, fully backward compatible with existing shows.

entries.summary: Fixed a real bug: OSC grandmaster fader input (/gma3/fader/PAGE/fdr) never matched its own dispatcher pattern -- dead since the day it was added
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (every item -- GUI polish, manual/glossary popup, changelog popup, fader FLASH-to-MIDI, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool panels -- already landed in prior sessions), so did a deep read of Block 11 (OSC Engine), which had never gotten a dedicated audit the way Blocks 7/9/12 did.

OSCEngine's own docstring and _osc_fader's docstring both document /gma3/fader/PAGE/fdr as a 2-segment address (e.g. /gma3/fader/1/1), and _osc_fader's own address-parsing code (parts[2]=page, parts[3]=fdr) matches that 4-token address. But the registration line read osc.map("/gma3/fader/*/*/*", _osc_fader) -- three wildcard segments, i.e. a 5-token pattern. OSC address-pattern matching (per the pythonosc dispatcher, which implements the OSC spec's segment-count-must-match rule) requires the same number of '/'-separated tokens on both sides; a 5-token pattern cannot match a 4-token address. Verified directly with pythonosc's own Dispatcher.call_handlers_for_packet(): a real /gma3/fader/1/1 message fell through to the default/unmapped handler and never reached _osc_fader, while /gma3/key/1/1/go (whose pattern correctly has 3 wildcards for a 3-segment PAGE/fdr/TYPE address) matched fine -- confirming the fader line was the only one wrong, not a systemic pattern-matching problem.

Checked git blame/log: this line has only ever been touched once, in the commit that introduced it -- so any MA3-style tool (Chataigne, TouchOSC, Bome) sending a fader move to Studio Console on port 8001 has never once been able to move the grandmaster dim via OSC, silently logged only as '(unmapped)' the whole time.

Fixed by dropping the extra wildcard segment: osc.map("/gma3/fader/*/*", _osc_fader). Verified the fix the same way the bug was found -- feeding a real built OSC packet through the actual dispatcher, not just calling the handler function directly.

Added a new smoke-test check that builds a real /gma3/fader/1/1 OSC packet with pythonosc's OscMessageBuilder and runs it through osc._dispatch.call_handlers_for_packet(), asserting the grandmaster dim (_fader_dim[0]) actually changes -- so a future regression in this pattern is caught by the automated suite instead of requiring another manual dispatcher trace.

One-line functional fix (plus one doc-comment tweak) + one new smoke-test check. No schema or persisted-data changes, fully backward compatible. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (43/43, 42 previous + 1 new); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

details: Every prior session's changelog entry that touched GUI layout flagged the same limitation: no display access, so sizing/clipping fixes were verified by code review only ('worth a visual check next time the console runs on a real screen', 'no pixel-level layout verification (can't screenshot)'). Found a real, previously invisible bug: _load_console_font() only ever tried to load '/System/Library/Fonts/SFNSMono.ttf' (macOS-only) and silently returned None everywhere else, falling back to DearPyGui's built-in bitmap font. That bitmap font has no glyphs for em/en dash, curly quotes, ellipsis, bullet, or the ▲▼◀▶■□●○ symbols used throughout the UI for status indicators and combo arrows — every one of them rendered as a literal '?'. Also removed the now-pointless add_font_range_hint/add_font_range calls from the old code — confirmed via DeprecationWarning that both are no-ops in dearpygui 2.3.1 ('character ranges are now automatic'), so a loaded font gets full glyph coverage for free; keeping them just printed warnings on every startup for nothing. Re-screenshotted the changelog, manual, MIDI, attribute-pool, fader-pages, patch, FX editor, monitors, color-picker, and AI-prompts popups after the fix — all render real dashes/quotes/arrows/shapes instead of '?' now.

Also found, via the same screenshot pass, a genuine sizing bug the roadmap explicitly calls out: the AI prompts popup (ai_prompts_window) was declared height=480 but its actual content (prompt grid + separator + label + multiline input + save-prompt button) needs more — the 'save prompt' button was rendered partially below the window's own bottom border. Bumped to height=520; re-screenshotted to confirm the button now sits fully inside the window with normal padding.

Backward compatible: on macOS with SF Mono present, behavior is unchanged (same font file, same size). On any OS with none of the candidate font files present, falls back to the exact same None/bitmap-font behavior as before — no new failure mode. No data-model or schema changes; studio_data/*.json untouched (verified: all GUI testing happened against a scratch copy in /tmp, never the real files, and git status after this session's edits shows only studio_project.py + this changelog entry touched). entries.summary: Hardened Block 9 (Audio Engine) startup: missing sounddevice/PortAudio no longer crashes the entire console
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (all 7 items already landed across prior sessions), so did a deep read of the one Block that had never gotten a dedicated audit: Block 9, Audio Engine (AudioEngine + AudioMapper). Grepped the whole file for AudioEngine/AudioMapper/audio_engine/audio_mapper usage outside Block 9 itself and found zero hits -- unlike every other Block, this one is fully implemented (RMS level + 3-band FFT analysis, attack/release envelope, a bass=red/mid=green/high=blue/level=dim mapper) but never instantiated, never given a command handler, never surfaced in the GUI, and not mentioned as a roadmap item. It is currently 100% dead code.

Found a real bug while confirming that:  at module level binds to the native PortAudio library at import time (unlike mido/rtmidi, which import lazily and only fail when a port is actually opened -- already hardened in Block 10). On a box without PortAudio installed, this raised a bare OSError and crashed the whole console before a single fixture patched, before the network/MIDI/OSC engines started, before the GUI could even build -- for a feature nothing else in the file uses. Reproduced directly: a fresh environment with sounddevice's Python package but no libportaudio2 failed with 'OSError: PortAudio library not found' at line 3183, killing the entire process.

Fixed by wrapping the sounddevice/numpy imports (numpy is also only used inside this Block) in a try/except that sets _AUDIO_AVAILABLE=False and stashes the error instead of propagating it. AudioEngine.list_devices() now prints a clear 'Audio engine unavailable (...)' message instead of raising when the backend is missing; AudioEngine.start() raises a clean RuntimeError with the underlying cause instead of an opaque OSError/ImportError. This mirrors the existing Block 10 pattern ('MIDI startup hardened against missing MIDI backend entirely').

Verified two ways: (1) simulated a genuinely missing sounddevice package via a sys.meta_path import blocker and confirmed the full STUDIO_DRY_RUN/STUDIO_HEADLESS smoke test now boots and passes end-to-end instead of crashing at import. (2) Added 2 new smoke-test checks that force _AUDIO_AVAILABLE=False directly (restored in a finally block) and assert list_devices() doesn't raise and start() raises RuntimeError specifically -- so this regression is caught automatically on every future run regardless of whether the CI/dev box happens to have a working audio stack installed, not just when someone thinks to test the missing-dependency case by hand.

NEEDS ALIGNMENT (not fixing without direction, flagging for the user like the attribute-pools entry did): AudioEngine/AudioMapper are fully built but entirely unwired -- no AUDIO ON/OFF command, no GUI toggle or level meters, no persistence of the audio-reactive mapping in show files. Options: (a) wire it up as a real feature (needs a command handler, a GUI panel with device picker + live level bars, and a decision on whether the bass/mid/high/level -> RGB/dim mapping should be user-configurable or stay hardcoded), (b) leave as dormant/optional code now that it can no longer crash startup, or (c) remove it entirely if audio-reactive lighting isn't wanted for this rig. This session only fixed the startup-crash bug and did not make a product decision to build out or remove the feature.

No schema or persisted-data changes -- pure import-time robustness fix, fully backward compatible with existing shows. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (42/42 smoke test, 40 previous + 2 new).

entries.summary: Fix: idle faders had no reachable FLASH button in the GUI (mouse-only operation was broken)
details: Roadmap item 'fader FLASH mode wired to actual MIDI press-and-hold' was marked done in prior changelogs, and the MIDI path (note-learn → fdr <n> FLASH ON/OFF) does work correctly. But the mouse-driven path was broken: _rebuild_playbacks() only ever created a flash_btn_{eid} widget for faders where `ex.is_active and ex.stack` was true. fader.is_active only flips to True inside go()/back()/goto()/reload()/flash_on(), and back to False in stop() (which flash_off() calls). Net effect: an fader that has a stack ASSIGNed but has never been GO'd — the normal starting state for something you intend to trigger only via FLASH — had no button to click at all, and flash_off() deletes the button again the instant it's released (is_active goes back to False, next rebuild drops the row). The command-line path (fdr <n> FLASH ON/OFF) always worked; only the physical/mouse control was unreachable for idle faders.

Fix: _rebuild_playbacks(), _playbacks_state_hash(), and the tick-loop's FLASH hold-detection (poll of is_item_active(flash_btn_{eid})) now all gate on `ex.stack` alone, not `ex.is_active and ex.stack`. The Playbacks panel now lists every fader that has a stack assigned, whether it's currently playing a cue or idle, ordered by fire-order first (most recently active) then remaining idle slots by fader number. Idle rows show '▶ —' for the cue label (cs.current is None until first GO), same as before — only the missing widget was the bug, not the labeling.

active_layers() (the actual DMX output merge) and the AI-context / LIST-command 'active faders' summaries were deliberately left untouched — those correctly mean 'currently contributing to output', which idle-but-assigned faders are not. Only the three GUI-surfacing spots changed.

Verified two ways: (1) STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test still 40/40. (2) New pixel-level check, not just code review this time — this container has Xvfb, so ran a scratch copy of the repo (own studio_data copy, real show untouched) under xvfb-run with dearpygui.dearpygui.start_dearpygui monkeypatched to run real render frames instead of blocking. Assigned a stack to an idle fader via ASSIGN stk 1 TO fdr 5 (never GO'd), rebuilt the playbacks panel, and confirmed flash_btn_5 now exists as a real widget and fader 5 is included in the tick loop's flash-hold poll set. Before this fix that widget would not have existed.
No schema or persisted-data changes — pure GUI/behavior fix over existing fader state. Backward compatible: no new fields, no changed save format.

entries.summary: Expanded smoke test to cover RECORD GROUP/FORM/FX + attribute pools (all passed); flagging attribute pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control) as dead code for this rig — needs a decision
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (all 7 items already landed across prior sessions), so instead of another deep-dive on a single Block, looked for untested-but-implemented command paths the way past sessions found real bugs in Block 7 and Block 12. Found several RECORD paths that had never been exercised by the smoke test: RECORD GROUP (+ GROUP recall), RECORD FORM (custom breakpoint curve) + FORM LIST, and RECORD FX + FIRE FX (roundtrip through the pool and back into the programmer).

Added 12 new smoke-test checks for those paths (2 for GROUP, 2 for FORM, 2 for FX, 6 for the attribute pools below). All passed on first run (one test-authoring mistake caught and fixed along the way: RECORD FORM title-cases its name argument, so a check for the literal string 'SmokeWave' needed to become a case-insensitive match — not a product bug). No new bugs found in GROUP/FORM/FX record/recall — that code is solid.

While adding coverage for the six attribute pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control — the GUI popup landed last session), traced why RECORD POSITION etc. always report 'no data in programmer': the patched fixture profile for all 6 units (SGM_RGB_54) only defines red/green/blue channels. There is no command anywhere in the file that writes pan, tilt, gobo, zoom, focus, iris, shutter, strobe, prism, frost, macro, or animation values into the programmer — grepped for 'AT PAN', 'AT GOBO', 'AT ZOOM' etc. and found zero hits. Even if such a command existed, SubFixture.get_dmx_values() only emits channels present in profile.channels, so non-RGB channel data could never reach DMX output for these fixtures regardless.

Net effect: the position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control pools and their GUI popup (the 'attr' button) are structurally unable to ever hold real data for this specific rig — 6 SGM LT-200 pixel tubes are static color fixtures with no moving parts, no gobos, no zoom/focus motors. Confirmed this is not a bug in the newly-added smoke test coverage (RECORD gracefully returns a clean 'no data' message rather than crashing, which the new checks now assert), it's a mismatch between a generic moving-light attribute framework built for a future/hypothetical fixture type and the actual patched hardware.

NEEDS ALIGNMENT — not fixing without direction: three options exist and picking one is a product decision, not a bug fix. (a) Leave as-is — harmless dead UI, costs nothing to keep if a moving fixture is ever patched later. (b) Repurpose control_pool specifically for real LT-200 attributes if the real fixture's DMX personality has anything beyond RGB (e.g. a strobe or macro channel) worth exposing — would need the actual LT-200 DMX chart to know what's available and correct to add. (c) Remove the pools/popup entirely as inapplicable to this show's patch. Leaving this for the user rather than guessing which of the three is wanted.
No schema or persisted-data changes. Verification: python3 -m py_compile passes; STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test passes 40/40 (28 previous + 12 new).

entries.summary: Fixed a real safety bug: BLACKOUT did not cut output for HIGHLIGHTed fixtures
details: Roadmap re-audit again found nothing new (all documented items already landed in prior sessions), so did a deep read of Block 7 (OutputState.get_dmx_for_universe) — the core DMX merge/output path — since it hadn't had a dedicated deep-dive changelog entry the way Block 12 (AI engine) got last session.

Found: the HIGHLIGHT branch in get_dmx_for_universe() set final_r/g/b = 255 unconditionally for highlighted fixtures, completely bypassing the grandmaster fader (gm = self.master_level). Every other output path (the non-highlight else branch) correctly multiplies by gm. Consequence: HIGHLIGHT ON followed by BLACKOUT (which just sets master_level = 0.0) left highlighted fixtures transmitting full white (255,255,255) on the real DMX/sACN line — BLACKOUT is documented and relied on as 'Cut all DMX output instantly', an absolute safety cutoff, and this silently violated that for any fixture still marked highlighted.

Fixed: highlighted fixtures now compute final_r/g/b = int(255 * gm) — full open white *relative to* the grandmaster position, matching how a real desk's highlight function behaves (it can never exceed where the master fader physically sits). Per-fixture dim is still bypassed by design (that's the point of highlight), only the grandmaster relationship was wrong.

Added a smoke-test check: ALL → HIGHLIGHT → BLACKOUT → assert max(dmx) == 0 on the real get_dmx_for_universe() output, not just the flags, so a future regression here is caught the same way it was found.
No schema or persisted-data changes — pure output-computation fix, fully backward compatible with existing shows.
Verification: python3 -m py_compile passes; STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test passes 28/28 (27 previous + 1 new).

entries.summary: Fixed 4 real bugs in the Block 12 AI engine: frozen stack snapshot, wrong stack->fader resolution, dead fade_time action, destructive fx_clear
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (same as every recent session — all 7 items already landed), so did a deep read of Block 12 specifically, since it's the area every prior session's audit checked only at a surface level ('AI actions dispatcher exists and looks complete') rather than tracing each action handler against the rest of the codebase. Found four real bugs, all previously undetected:

(1) AIEngine was constructed with `stacks={1: cs1}` — a frozen dict snapshot taken once at startup — instead of a live reference to stack_pool. cs2/cs3 exist in stack_pool from the same startup block, so the AI was permanently blind to them, and nothing ever updated the snapshot (not LOAD SHOW, not RECORD stk 2, not GUI stack creation). Fixed: AIEngine now takes stack_pool directly and _state() reads .stacks live, so it always reflects current state including after LOAD SHOW.

(2) Every cue-fire action (goto_cue/cue_go/cue_back/cue_fire) resolved the AI's 'stack' parameter via fader_pool.get(stack_id) — treating a stack id as if it were an fader slot id. Since faderPool.get() auto-creates missing slots, this silently fired whatever (possibly wrong, possibly empty) fader happened to share that number, the moment a stack was assigned to a differently-numbered fader (e.g. ASSIGN stk 2 TO fdr 9) — masked until now only by the default 1:1 startup wiring. Any 'fader N: no stack assigned' failure was also discarded, never logged. Fixed: new _exec_for_stack() searches actual fader->stack assignments first, falling back to same-numbered slot only if none found; _fire() now logs every fire result including failures.

(3) fade_time set self._last_fade but nothing ever read that field — fully documented in ACTION_SCHEMA, fully inert. The AI could be asked for a slow fade into a cue and would report the action as executed while nothing happened. Fixed: _fire() now consumes a pending fade_time once, applying it as a temporary fader time-override for the very next cue-fire action in the same batch (same restore-after pattern as the existing fader.flash_on()), then clears it — not a standing default.

(4) fx_clear and fx_stop-with-no-channel called fx_engine.clear() directly. FXEngine.clear() wipes every layer including ones owned by running cue faders (whose ids go stale in ex._fx_ids), and — unlike the real 'FX CLEAR' command handler — never pops the programmer's pending 'fx' defs, so the next programmer-FX rebuild tick could resurrect them. Both actions now route through self._cmd('FX CLEAR'), matching command-line behavior exactly.

Verification: python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 both pass (27/27, unaffected since the smoke test never sets an API key so this code never runs there). Went further than that this time: built a scratch harness with a fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to call ai.execute() directly and check all four fixes against real objects — live stack visibility, correct fader resolution after a stack was reassigned away from its default fader, single-use fade_time consumption, and fx_clear actually clearing programmer fx defs. All 6/6 checks passed. That harness also turned up a real but unrelated hazard worth flagging for future sessions: calling ai._log (== gui._log, which calls dpg.set_value on the 'cmd_log' tag) from headless mode segfaults dearpygui's C extension, because gui.build() — which creates that widget — never runs in STUDIO_HEADLESS. Confirmed this is not reachable by real users (the GUI is always built before any AI action can be triggered interactively), so left unfixed, but any future session adding headless-mode coverage of AI logging should route around gui._log or build a stub.
No schema or persisted-data changes — pure internal AIEngine wiring, fully backward compatible with existing shows.

details: Roadmap re-audit before touching anything: with the roadmap items all marked done in prior sessions' changelog entries, went looking for a concrete, verifiable bug instead — same pattern the last few sessions used. Confirmed this container has Xvfb + a working dearpygui import under `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24"` (per the technique a prior session documented), so did a full sweep: built the GUI on a scratch copy of the repo under STUDIO_DRY_RUN, opened every popup one at a time via a monkeypatched dpg.start_dearpygui, and captured dpg.output_frame_buffer() screenshots of each — main window plus all 9 floating popups (patch, osc, midi, fx editor, keys/manual, changelog, pages, monitors, color picker).

Main window at 1920x1040 and 8 of the 9 popups rendered cleanly with no clipping. Found two real, previously-undetected sizing bugs in the other two: (1) the color picker popup (_build_color_picker_popup) was fixed at width=310 height=390, but the color wheel widget alone measures 351x313px and the full stack of controls (wheel + R/G/B/hex readout + Apply/White/Off buttons + 8 quick-color swatches + status line) needs ~470px — confirmed via dpg.get_item_pos/get_item_rect_size that the last widget (cpick_status) sits at y=451, past the window's 390px height. (2) The manual/keys popup's command-reference table used plain dpg.add_text with no wrap= for the command-string column, so long command shorthand rows — e.g. '1 AT YELLOW / ORANGE / PINK / PURPLE / LIME / TEAL' — were silently cut off mid-word with no way to read the rest; this affected several of the longer named-colour and LIST rows.

Fixed by (1) resizing color_picker_window to 370x480 — verified via a fresh screenshot that Apply/White/Off and all 8 quick swatches now render fully visible with zero scrolling needed — and (2) adding wrap=280 (cmd column) / wrap=380 (desc column) to the keys-popup table's add_text calls, so long command strings now wrap onto a second line instead of being truncated — verified via a fresh screenshot showing the full 'YELLOW / ORANGE / PINK / PURPLE / LIME / TEAL' string wrapped and readable.

Both are pure sizing/cosmetic tweaks — no schema, data model, or command-handler changes, so no backward-compatibility concerns. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (27/27 smoke test); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json in the real repo was untouched (all screenshot verification ran against a throwaway copy in the scratch dir, never studio_data/popup_layout.json or any other real show file).

This closes out the one remaining open thread on the 'GUI polish: fix any sizing/clipping issues' roadmap item that every prior session had to leave flagged as 'can't verify without a real display' — this session's screenshot sweep covered all 9 popups plus the main window and found these were the only two with real clipping.

entries.summary: Fixed: cue tooltip computed FX layer count but never displayed it (dead variable, wrong key)
details: Roadmap check this session: re-read the full established roadmap (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, fader FLASH-to-MIDI, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool GUI panels) against the current code and changelog history — every item is already implemented by prior sessions (MIDI mapping popup has learn/direct-add/reassign/delete; FLASH is wired to real MIDI note on/off via off_callback; attribute pool panels exist for position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam with right-click Record/Apply/Rename/Clear). No functional gap found there, so this session looked for a concrete bug instead.

Found one via pyflakes ('local variable nfx is assigned to but never used') in the cue-pool tooltip builder (_tick_pools, cue slot loop): `nfx = len(cue.data.get('__fx__', []))` computed a value that was never interpolated into the tooltip string. Worse, the key itself was wrong — grep across the file confirms FX layers are stored per-fixture at `cue.data[fixture_id]['fx']` (see the FX ARCHITECTURE comment near the bottom of the file), never under a top-level '__fx__' key, so `nfx` was always 0 even before the dead-code issue — this line has never worked.

Fixed by summing `len(v.get('fx', []))` over every per-fixture dict entry in cue.data and appending a '\nN FX layer(s)' line to the tooltip (same pattern as the existing fixture-count line), so hovering a cue slot in the pool now actually shows how many FX layers that cue will fire on GO, matching what RECORD CUE already captures.

One-line-scope fix, no schema/data changes, fully backward compatible. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (8/8 smoke test); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

entries.summary: Fixed: AI bar and header 'ai' button were shown even without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, permanently busting the 1920x1080 layout budget
details: Real bug, not just documentation: `ai = AIEngine(...)` is always constructed and passed into GUIEngine as `self._ai`, so `if self._ai:` (used to gate both the header 'ai' button and the whole AI prompt bar) was always true — AIEngine has no __bool__/__len__, so a plain instance is always truthy regardless of its self._enabled flag. Every user, not just ones with an API key configured, was getting the AI bar built and the 'ai' header button shown, even though the AI engine internally refuses to do anything (ask() just prints 'set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY first') and the manual popup explicitly documents 'AI bar/buttons are hidden entirely if it isn't set'. Fixed both gates to check `self._ai and self._ai._enabled` instead of bare truthiness.

This also directly serves the 'GUI polish / fit in 1920x1080 with no scrollbars' roadmap item: the layout-budget comment above GUIEngine explicitly carves out the ~70px AI bar as 'the one section not counted' in the 980/988px budget, with the main window's scrollbar left on specifically as a fallback for that overflow case. Because the gate was always true, that fallback was silently engaged for 100% of users, not just the minority with an API key set — this fix makes the no-scrollbar case (no AI key, the default) actually achievable again, and confines the documented AI-bar-overflow tradeoff to only the sessions that opted into it.

New verification capability this session: got dearpygui actually rendering under this container's Xvfb (segfaulted at first — fixed with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 and an explicit `-screen 0 1920x1080x24` xvfb-run arg) and captured real screenshots via dpg.output_frame_buffer() from a frame callback (must be called after a few rendered frames, not immediately after show_viewport — 'Render loop must have been started'). This is a genuine step up from every prior session's 'can't verify pixel-exact without a real display' caveat. Verified with actual screenshots, on a scratch copy of the repo (never the real studio_data/*.json): (1) with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no AI bar and no 'ai' header button, main window fits with no visible scrollbar; (2) with a fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, both appear and the bar fits without visible clipping; (3) spot-checked the manual, MIDI mapping, and attribute-pools popups opened individually — all render cleanly with correct sizing, no clipped content.

Process note for future sessions: this screenshot technique (copy repo to scratch dir, monkeypatch dpg.start_dearpygui with a frame-counted callback that calls dpg.output_frame_buffer() then dpg.stop_dearpygui(), run under `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24"`) works in this container and should be reached for instead of static code reading whenever a change might affect layout — it would have caught this bug immediately.

Also noticed while auditing the changelog for context: the most recent commit before this session (2773932, 'add OSC target management GUI popup and persist targets to disk') has no corresponding changelog entry — a gap in a prior session's own record-keeping, left as-is here since it's not this session's change to document after the fact.

entries.summary: Fix OSC fader/key handlers silently dropping every fader except Page 1 fdr 1
details: Re-audited the established roadmap first (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, MIDI-held FLASH, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool panels) -- all confirmed already landed by prior sessions via direct code inspection, not just trusting the changelog. Ran a background research pass over the whole file (dead code, manual-vs-parser mismatches, MIDI/OSC symmetry, attribute pool CRUD parity) looking for the next real gap rather than re-doing finished work.

Found one: _osc_fader and _osc_key (the /gma3/fader/PAGE/fdr and /gma3/key/PAGE/fdr/TYPE MA3-style OSC input handlers) parsed page and fdr_num out of the incoming OSC address correctly, but then gated all actual behavior on 'if page == 1 and fdr_num == 1' -- a placeholder from when the console only had one fader wired up ('We map Page 1 fdr 1 -> grandmaster dim for now'). Every other fader was parsed, logged to console, and silently dropped, despite the console fully supporting many faders via the existing fdr <n> GO/BACK/LEVEL command family that MIDI targets already use freely.

_osc_fader now keeps the legacy Page 1 fdr 1 -> grandmaster-dim mapping (so existing OSC templates don't change behavior) but routes any other page/fdr straight to that fader's own .level field -- the same field the GUI fader sliders write via _on_exec_fader, and written directly (no save_show() call) so a fast fader sweep doesn't hammer disk I/O on every OSC message, matching how the GUI slider already behaves.

_osc_key keeps Page 1 fdr 1 Go/Back mapped to the active fader (cue_go()/cue_back(), unchanged) but routes any other page/fdr through run_command('fdr <n> GO') or 'fdr <n> BACK' -- the identical command path the text command line and MIDI note targets use, so a TouchOSC/Chataigne page can now drive any fader, not just the first one.

This console does not have grandMA3-style paging of fader numbers (PAGE here organizes stacks for display only, per faderPool.pages -- confirmed while investigating, does not affect playback), so 'page' in the OSC address is accepted for compatibility with MA3-shaped OSC templates but otherwise ignored; fdr_num alone selects the fader.

Smoke test extended: dispatches real /gma3/fader/1/3 and /gma3/key/1/3/go packets through osc._dispatch.call_handlers_for_packet() (not just calling the handler functions directly) and confirms fader 3 -- which is wired to stack 3 by the default 1:1 startup assignment -- receives its own level and actually GOes, while leaving the existing Page 1 fdr 1 grandmaster-dim test untouched. 61/61 passing (59 previous + 2 new). Verified studio_data/*.json untouched via git status.
No schema or persisted-data changes -- pure bugfix in existing OSC dispatch code, fully backward compatible.

entries.summary: Fixed a real bug: FX Pool presets silently lost their SpeedMaster link (speed_id) on every save/load cycle
details: Re-audited the established roadmap first (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, MIDI-held FLASH, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool panels) -- all confirmed already landed. Two prior 'NEEDS ALIGNMENT' items remain open and were deliberately left alone rather than guessed on: (1) whether the attribute pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control) should be repurposed, left dormant, or removed for this RGB-only rig, and (2) whether the MIDI/OSC Grandmaster Dim control should scale output like MASTER does instead of stamping an absolute per-fixture dim. Both still need a product decision from the user, not a code fix.

Spawned a background research pass auditing Block 14 (Show File Persistence) end-to-end -- a full pair-by-pair save_X/load_X field audit, since persistence round-trip asymmetry (a field written in one place but forgotten in its mirror) has been this codebase's most common real-bug pattern. Also verified the most recent commit (CLEAR COLOUR/DIM/FX writing explicit zeros so they're recordable into cues) round-trips correctly end to end -- Cue.record, save_stacks/load_stacks, _resolve_cue_refs, and Fade.tick all treat an explicit 0 as present data, not as missing, so that path is correct.

Found a real bug in a different corner of the same Block: FXPreset.add_layer() has fully supported a speed_id field for several sessions (links an FX layer to one of the 16 SpeedMaster slots so it tracks live BPM instead of a fixed rate -- both the FX editor GUI's Speed dropdown and FXPreset.fire() use it correctly), but ShowFile.save_fx_pool()/load_fx_pool() -- the pair actually used by SAVE SHOW / LOAD SHOW -- never read or wrote that field. Saving a preset with a SpeedMaster link and restarting (or LOAD SHOW) silently reverted every linked layer to its raw stored bpm, with no error or warning.

Same omission found at two more call sites that construct FXPreset objects from stored data: the RECORD FX <n> command handler (also missing phase_offset, so RECORD FX was additionally flattening any non-zero phase offset back to 0.0), and the IMPORT PRESETS bundle merge path (missing dim_id, color_id, and group_id as well as speed_id -- the widest gap of the three, since EXPORT PRESETS itself is fine, it round-trips fx_pool.json verbatim). Fixed all three call sites plus the save/load pair itself -- four call sites total, all now forwarding the complete field set that FXPreset.add_layer() actually accepts.

Smoke test extended: a direct save_fx_pool -> fresh FXPool -> load_fx_pool round-trip asserting speed_id survives, plus a RECORD FX check that a programmer FX def carrying speed_id ends up on the stored preset. 109/109 passing (106 previous + 3 new). Verified studio_data/*.json untouched via git status.

No schema changes to existing saved fields -- speed_id was already a valid, defaulted (None) parameter everywhere it was missing, so old fx_pool.json files and old show saves load exactly as before; the only change is that a speed_id now written going forward is no longer silently discarded on the next load.

Color pool buttons now show the preset's actual color as a background tint (dark resting / mid hover / full-bright active). Empty slots revert to default.
Dim pool buttons now show a brightness-scaled blue tint and a tooltip with the preset name and level %.
Left-column stack title replaced by a clickable combo — select any stack from the dropdown to switch the active cue list instantly.
Keyboard shortcuts added: Cmd/Ctrl+S saves the show; F5 fires GO; F4 fires BACK. Ctrl/Cmd+letter combos no longer accidentally append to the command input.

entries.summary: MIDI startup hardened against missing MIDI backend entirely (not just missing device)
details: Found while re-verifying the headless smoke test in a fresh container: MIDIEngine.list_ports() and start() both called mido.get_input_names() unguarded. That call raises an rtmidi-internal exception (not OSError/IOError, so the existing 'no port found' handling didn't catch it) when there's no ALSA/CoreMIDI backend available at all — e.g. a container with no /dev/snd/seq — as opposed to a backend that's present but has zero devices plugged in. Previously this crashed the whole app at import time, before the GUI or dry-run pipeline ever started.
Both call sites now catch broadly and print a 'MIDI backend unavailable' message, continuing without MIDI — same fallback behavior as the existing 'no device plugged in' and 'bad port index' cases.
STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test: 8/8 passing after the fix.

Note for the user, not a decision that needs one: this session also attempted the same 'Attribute pool GUI panels' roadmap item and found another session had already landed it (commits 887b10f/de4f3e9) with a different design — 5 always-visible panel rows in the main pools section rather than a popup. Discarded the duplicate rather than merge two designs. Flagging a real but unverified risk in that landed design: rows 4-5 add roughly two more 78px panel rows (~160px) to the main window's stacked content, on top of a layout that a prior session already flagged as tight for 1920x1080 (see the 'partial sizing fix' entry above, also unverified for the same reason — no display/screenshot access in this environment). The main window already has scrolling enabled as a fallback so this shouldn't crash or clip unreachably, but it likely means a visible scrollbar now where the roadmap goal was none. Worth a visual check next time the console runs on a real screen.

entries.summary: Visual polish: RGB-tinted bars, tap tempo, fade progress, BLIND/BLACKOUT, new commands
details: Output monitor and programmer monitor progress bars now tint to the fixture's actual RGB color — a red fixture shows a red bar, blue shows blue. Themes are cached and only rebuilt when the color changes.
Tap tempo button added to the FX section label row. Click it repeatedly to set BPM from tap intervals (auto-resets after 3s gap). Rate BPM slider and all live FX layers update immediately.

Each active fader row in the playbacks panel now shows a 4px amber fade progress bar below the level fader. Fills from 0→100% during a crossfade with overlay text showing percentage and total seconds. FadeEngine.fade_progress() added to expose this without touching internal state.

BLIND command suppresses the programmer layer from DMX output while keeping it visible in the monitors and stage preview — safe editing without affecting the live output. LIVE restores it. Red status bar indicator shows when active.

BLACKOUT command cuts master_level to 0.0 instantly, saving the pre-blackout level for restore. BLACKOUT OFF or a second BLACKOUT restores. BBO is a one-key alias. Red '■ BBO' status bar indicator. Master fader in stage panel syncs to 0.
SNAPSHOT <n> [name] records the full current live look (cue + programmer merged, across all running faders) as a standalone cue. Unlike RECORD CUE which only records programmer content.
DELETE CUE <n> [stk <m>] removes a cue from a stack and saves the show. The underlying stack.delete_cue() method already existed but was never exposed via command parser.
CUE <n> SHOW prints a summary of what's stored in a specific cue: fade/delay times, per-fixture dim and FX defs, and a compact per-color count of sub-fixture pixel values.
GOTO and ASSIGN stk <n> TO fdr <n> documented in command reference. Keyboard shortcut reference updated with F5/F4/Cmd+S and tap tempo. RENAME/COPY section renamed RENAME/COPY/DELETE.

entries.summary: fader Pages GUI panel + command manual documentation gaps
details: Audited the roadmap against the current file before touching anything: GUI polish (scroll fallback), manual popup, changelog popup, MIDI-held FLASH, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, and attribute pool panels were all already landed by prior sessions. Went looking for the next real gap instead of re-doing finished work.

Found one: faderPool.pages (PAGE <n> NAME/ADD/REMOVE/LIST) existed only as a data model + command-line verb, with zero GUI surface — the one pool-like feature that hadn't gotten the popup treatment the MIDI mapping and patch editors already have.

Added a 'pages' header button opening a new fader Pages popup: a live table of page number / name / assigned faders, plus rename-page and add/remove-fader-from-page controls. Pure GUI front-end over the existing PAGE command handlers — no changes to faderPool, no playback behavior touched (pages remain organizational-only, as already documented in the code).

Also found the command manual (the '?' popup) was missing docs for CLEAR COLOR/DIM/GROUP/FX <n> (pool-slot deletion, added in an earlier session) — added those four entries plus a 'PAGES button' row in KEYBOARD and faderS & PAGES sections.

No data model or schema changes — nothing new to persist, so no backward-compatibility concerns. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (8/8 smoke test). Note: gui.build() itself (the actual DPG window/table construction) still can't be exercised in this environment — no display access — so the new popup's widget code is unverified beyond close review against the existing MIDI/patch/changelog popups it mirrors line-for-line in structure.
